newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers eight blocks in 1997 oil search round.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers eight blocks in 1997 oil search round.

text.p: Egypt is offering eight oil concessions in its 1997 exploration round, two for bids by March 31 and six for bids by September 30.
The eight blocks together cover an area of 156,000 square km (60,000 square miles), about a sixth of Egypt's total area, the state's Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) said on Monday.
Those offered for bids by March 31 are:

-- North Ras Qattara, 530 square km onshore west of Alexandria. The block is in two non-contiguous sections, one on the Mediterranean coast and one inland in the Western Desert, on the northwestern edge of the Qattara Depression.
-- North Bahariya, 823 square km, also in the Western Desert and near the oasis of Bahariya.
Those for bids by September 30 are:

-- Two adjacent offshore blocks off the northwestern coast, extending up to 200 km into the Mediterrean. One, West Mediterranean Deep Water A, is 21,600 square km, and the other, West Mediterranean Deep Water B, is 15,600 square km.
-- Siwa, 15,600 square km near Siwa oasis, touching the Libyan border.
-- Assiut, 34,712 square km around the southern city of the same name.
-- North West Gemsa, 825 square km on the western shores of the Gulf of Suez, near the village of Gemsa.
-- North El Mesaha Trough, the largest block, 62,987 square km touching the Sudanese border and roughly half way between the Nile Valley and the Libyan border.
EGPC said oil companies including Amoco had drilled five wells in the North Bahariya block since 1968. Other data on this or the other blocks were not immediately available.
